title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a compact sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and reinforcement learning agents without depending on ROS. It provides native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution across common robot arms including Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101, making it useful for researchers who want a lighter path from simulation experiments to real robot control.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable setup for building robot simulation environments from interchangeable robots, objects, and task scenes. It is aimed at quickly prototyping robotics tasks and evaluating learned policies across different embodiments and environments, making it useful for scalable simulation experiments rather than one-off task definitions.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: IsaacLab DirectEnv setup for training and testing basic quadruped locomotion policies across multiple robot platforms. It is aimed at the practical pipeline around locomotion research, including sim-to-sim transfer and sim-to-real deployment, so it looks useful as a starting point for comparing robots and moving policies out of IsaacLab into other simulators or hardware.

summary: RoboVerse aims to unify robot learning infrastructure by packaging a platform, dataset, and benchmark around scalable, generalizable robot behavior. It is meant to give researchers a common place to build and evaluate robot learning methods across tasks, reducing the usual fragmentation between simulation, data collection, and benchmarking.

title: iLearn-Lab/CVPR26-OptimusVLA
summary: OptimusVLA is the official implementation of a CVPR 2026 vision-language-action model for robotic manipulation that combines a global prior with local consistency through a dual-memory design. The interesting part is the memory mechanism: it augments action generation with broader task-level context while preserving locally coherent manipulation behavior, aiming to make robot control more efficient and reliable.
